Silas Vance.narrative: I have worked stone since I was a lad, and I have been foreman on the ridge long enough to know a bad cut before the hammer falls. When Ezra picked that line across the cairn stones I told him the ground looked wrong, and he went ahead anyway; I will not take a crew back up there, not for Josiah Crane nor for the Council. My wife Odile says the giants are owed an answer, and I reckon she is right, but the answer is Ezra's to give, not mine. I keep the quarry floor below the ridge and my house by the clock tower, and I will not be shamed into climbing again.
values: an honest day's work for an honest day's pay
a foreman's word is his bond
goals: keep my crew off the ridge and my name clear of the cutting
see Ezra stand up and answer for the cairn
hold my foreman's place under Josiah Crane
get Corwin to look higher than a terrace farmer's daughter
Silas Vance.mood: grim and set in his ways

relations.name: Odile Vance
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She says what I will not say aloud, and she is usually right about it.

relations.name: Corwin Vance
relations.label: son
relations.note: A good hand with stone, but he thinks a foreman's place is owed him and a farmer's girl is good enough.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: quarryman
relations.note: He chose the ridge and now he will not climb it. The answer is his to give, and he gives it to Josiah instead of the giants.

relations.name: Corin Holt
relations.label: quarryman's wife
relations.note: She keeps the tally straight and does not spare her husband at home. I can respect that.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: master
relations.note: He pays my wage and presses me to press Ezra. I will not be pressed up that ridge.

relations.name: Ambrose Vell
relations.label: council master
relations.note: Slow to speak and slower to forgive. He would not send a crew up there either.

relations.name: Hedley Ashcombe
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A terrace farmer with opinions about quarrymen. His daughter is the one Corwin has set his heart on.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: clockkeeper
relations.note: He writes the contracts and winds the clock. A man who keeps things in order.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: builder
relations.note: He builds the seawall crates and grumbles about the stone price like the rest of them.

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: Works cheap and the yard mutters. He has not been up the ridge either, so he does not know what he is cheap about.

relations.name: Rosalind Ashcombe
relations.label: son's sweetheart
relations.note: A hard worker on poor ground, and that counts for something. But a foreman's son can look higher than a terrace strip, and I have said it once too often already.

memories.gist: The morning Ezra chose the line across the ridge and I told him the ground looked wrong; he laughed and set the first drill.
The day the drill broke into the cairn stones and the whole crew went quiet, and I knew we had done something that could not be undone.
Josiah Crane in the Council yard telling me to take a crew back up and finish the ridge order, and me saying no to his face.
Odile setting a quarryman's arm by the clock tower while I held the man still, and her telling me afterwards that the cairn cutting was a sin.
Corwin at the supper table saying his father had gone soft about the ridge, and me leaving the table rather than strike him.
The Lean Year, when the works went short and the quarry crews took half wages and the terrace families queued at the works' kitchen.

stances.why: I told Ezra the ground was wrong and I will not take men up there to prove it again.
He chose the line. The giants are owed an answer, and it is not mine to give.
A foreman who loses men to his own pride is no foreman.
A foreman's son can do better than a terrace farmer's daughter, and I have said so once too often.
The masters sit in the yard and set the price; it is the crews that take the risk.

Odile Vance.narrative: I keep the healer's room by the clock tower, and quarrymen come to me with broken fingers and crushed feet and I set them as best I can. I buy my herbs from a Tanglewood woman who walks the old forest paths, and she has taught me more than the works' doctors ever did. When they cut into the cairn I said in my own house and to anyone who asked that it was wrong, and I have not changed my mind; the giants keep their dead on the ridges and we had no business there. Silas will not go back up and I do not press him, though Josiah Crane presses him enough for both of us.
values: heal whoever comes to the door
the dead are not to be disturbed
a healer keeps her own counsel
herbs and patience over the works' doctors
goals: keep the quarry crews mending and the salves stocked through winter
see the cairn cutting answered for, and the giants' peace mended if it can be
keep Silas from being driven up the ridge by the Council
see Corwin settle with a girl who will not make him a stranger in his own house

relations.name: Silas Vance
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He carries the ridge on his shoulders and will not say so. I set his hands when the stone splits them.

relations.name: Corwin Vance
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has his father's stubbornness and none of his patience. I wish he would stop measuring himself against Silas.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: quarryman
relations.note: Careless is the kindest word I have for it. He should have known what the stones were.

relations.name: Corin Holt
relations.label: quarryman's wife
relations.note: She says at home what I say in my room, and it costs her. I send her salve for her hands.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: master
relations.note: He wants the ridge stone and does not care what was disturbed to get it.

relations.name: Odile Wrack
relations.label: fellow healer
relations.note: A Kettlebridge woman gone down to the quay. We trade herbs and complaints when she comes up.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: fellow healer
relations.note: She sets bones on the quay and buys from the same Tanglewood woman. I would trust her with a bad break.

relations.name: Hedley Ashcombe
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A decent man with a daughter who works hard. Silas is wrong about her.

relations.name: Rosalind Ashcombe
relations.label: neighbour's daughter
relations.note: She came to me for a salve for her father's knees and stayed to talk of the poor strip. A good girl.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: Brings me herbs and news from the road. His back is bad and he will not rest it.

relations.name: Mabel Fenwick
relations.label: stallkeeper
relations.note: Sells me ironware and works' seconds and never cheats the weight.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: clockkeeper
relations.note: Writes a clean hand and keeps the clock honest. I have him copy my salve lists.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: herb-seller
relations.note: Her salves are honest and her roots are sound. She left the chapel and will not come back through the gate, and I cannot say I blame her.

memories.gist: The week the crews came down from the ridge with their hands shaking, and I set three broken fingers in one evening and heard the same story each time.
Telling Silas at our own table that the cairn cutting was a sin, and him not arguing, only sitting with his cup.
The Tanglewood woman showing me how to draw the fever out of a quarryman's cut with a poultice of old forest leaves.
Corwin bringing Rosalind Ashcombe to the door for a salve and watching her like a lad at a fair, and me pretending not to notice.
The Lean Year, when half the terrace came to my room with coughs and no marks to pay, and I took what they could give and no more.

stances.why: The giants keep their dead on the ridges and we had no business there. I have said so and will say so again.
A healer who asks a man's quarrel before she sets his bone is no healer.
He told Ezra the ground was wrong and was not heard. I will not be the one who drives him back up.
Hollbrenna closed the shelf for a reason, and someone should go and speak to her plainly.
Silas has said his piece once too often. The boy will marry where he will, and Rosalind is no bad choice.

Corwin Vance.narrative: I work the quarry floor under Ezra Holt and I am not ashamed of it, but I mean to have my father's foreman's place and I do not see why wanting it should be a sin. My father will not go back up the ridge and the crews mutter about it; I think a foreman who will not climb is no foreman, cairn or no cairn. Rosalind Ashcombe is the best thing in my life and her father looks at me like I am the tithe collector come round, and my own father looks at her like she is beneath us, and neither of them has asked me what I want.
values: a man makes his own place
the crew respects a foreman who climbs
hard work and a fair wage
goals: take my father's foreman's place on the ridge
marry Rosalind Ashcombe with both fathers' blessing, or without them
get the ridge crews working again so the Lanternquay order is met
prove to Silas that I am not a boy to be told who to court

relations.name: Silas Vance
relations.label: father
relations.note: He thinks I am soft for wanting the ridge worked and soft for wanting Rosalind. I am neither.

relations.name: Odile Vance
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She does not lecture me. She asks questions and then sets my hands when the stone splits them.

relations.name: Rosalind Ashcombe
relations.label: sweetheart
relations.note: She wants to try a new crop on the poor strip and I would dig the whole terrace for her.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: crew boss
relations.note: He chose the ridge and he will not climb it, and the crews pay for it. A foreman should climb.

relations.name: Hedley Ashcombe
relations.label: her father
relations.note: He looks at me like the tithe collector. I have never taken a thing from his strips.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: master
relations.note: He wants the ridge stone and the crews up there. He does not care that my father will not go.

relations.name: Bisi Oyelaran
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Quick with numbers and quick with her tongue. She minds her mother's stall and wants the foundry books.

relations.name: Corin Holt
relations.label: crew wife
relations.note: She keeps the tally and does not spare Ezra at home. I like her for it.

relations.name: Lottie Fenwick
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She minds her father's stall and has a good eye for a cracked pot, and she does not care whose father says what.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: Hauls our stone north and hates the gate-due. He knows the road better than the Council does.

memories.gist: My first day on the quarry floor under Ezra, and my father watching from the lip of the cut without a word.
The crews coming down from the ridge after the cairn was cut, and the talk of it in the yard, and my father saying he would not go back up.
Rosalind Ashcombe laughing at something I said at the square stall, and me walking her back to the terrace steps and not wanting to go home.
Supper at our table when my father said a foreman's son could do better than a farmer's daughter, and my mother set down her spoon and said nothing.
The clock striking noon over the square while I counted the loads on the quarry cart and thought that one day the tally would be mine to keep.

stances.why: A foreman who will not go up the ridge is no foreman, whatever the crews mutter about the cairn.
Josiah needs the ridge stone for the Lanternquay order, and the works cannot eat pride.
Neither her father nor mine has asked me what I want, and I want her.
He will not climb and he will not say why beyond the cairn. The crews notice.
Bisi and Lottie and Rosalind are worth more than the masters' opinions of them.
